data.narrative:
Runpod, a Series C semiconductor company founded by Zhen Lu and Pardeep Singh, has raised $122.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage companies in chips and semiconductors, including same-stage comparables DEEPX ($529M), Positron AI ($1.0B), and Tenstorrent ($2.7B).

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $208M. Peer-median analysis across the same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables produces $1.0B, with a range spanning $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (20.5x median across the semiconductor peer set) cannot be applied absent revenue disclosure, common for private companies at this stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $177M to $1.1B, with a median of $604M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around stage-comparable selection and the absence of revenue-based valuation methods. Key downside risks center on execution relative to better-capitalized peers; upside depends on differentiation in inference efficiency or cost structure versus the peer set. Additional disclosure of go-to-market traction or unit economics would narrow this range materially.
